# Speed of the encryption of one peer message, per AEAD
What: ns to seal one message (encrypt and tag) and ns to open it (check and decrypt), each in its own loop.
Input: one message of 64 B, 1 KiB or 64 KiB, filled with i*131+7. 512 KiB per sample, at least 16 messages; 31 samples per run; 3 rounds, binaries run alternately.
Arms: aes256gcm and aes256gcm_aa (OpenSSL EVP AES-256-GCM, 12-byte counter IV, 16-byte tag, one EVP_CIPHER_CTX per direction; aa is the noise floor), chacha20poly1305 (OpenSSL EVP), hydro (libhydrogen hydro_secretbox_encrypt/decrypt, tree deps/libhydrogen, message id = counter).
Builds: Release, C++23, one binary per arm and compiler. libhydrogen built by its own CMake with HYDROGEN_TARGET_ARCH x86-64.
Container: podman --cpus=3 on 4 processors, image localhost/hashbench. Run as user bench (uid 1001), not root, not pinned.
Source digests (sha256): bench.cpp 78d90988032334948cc9ffac2ebabf402fd7d244820c7dff070fff85b78c2c64 CMakeLists.txt b76f6475a987ce78fa94c8ce1f23cee8ebc8faa0c89468350a9dd0fb824645d5 run-inside.sh 2b5afb02959f281ef14a64320b5039a60ca5ca0964f0f9a521bd7e84d2173414
deps/libhydrogen 264bf42
Host: 6.18.44-fc-v185, VM Firecracker, Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor, flags aes vaes pclmulqdq avx2 avx512f present
